title: Signal Gatekeeper: trace-hook enrichment, metric/log fusion, and autoresolve playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We continue to see noisy burn-rate pages from the runtime tier where trace-less errors and metric spikes cause over-eager paging. This ticket implements the 'Signal Gatekeeper' — a combined tracing-hook enrichment + metrics/logs fusion layer and an autoresolve/autosnooze playbook to reduce noise while preserving SLO fidelity.

Goals:
- Improve signal quality for SLO burn-rate alerts by enriching traces with request routing and model-variant metadata at the ingress tracing hook.
- Fuse metrics and recent logs to validate whether a burn-rate spike represents a true degradation or transient noise (e.g., single-customer retry storms).
- Implement adaptive autoresolve/autosnooze rules and a guided human-in-the-loop escalation flow to reduce pagers by ~40% without increasing SLI error budgets beyond 5%.

Scope (what we'll deliver in this ticket):
- Add an entry-point trace hook that tags requests with: customer_id, model_variant_id, routing_policy, and inferred_user_intent when available. Hook outputs follow our tracing schema v2.
- Build a streaming correlator that joins recent high-cardinality metrics (error_rate, latency_p50/p95/p99) with tail logs over a 2-minute window and emits a fused 'signal_confidence' metric.
- New alert processor rules that consult 'signal_confidence' before firing SLO paging: allow conditional suppression, aggregated paging, or immediate page.
- Autoresolve/autosnooze playbook implementation with audit logs and an override path for SREs.
- Dashboard and runbook updates: latency/error dashboards with per-customer heatmap, a 'signal health' panel, and an incident checklist.

Out of scope for this ticket:
- Full ML-backed anomaly retraining (we will ship a heuristic hybrid initially).
- Cross-region historical reanalysis (future work).

Acceptance criteria:
- Trace hook deployed behind a feature flag and samples the new tags for 100% of dedicated and 20% of hosted requests.
- Fused 'signal_confidence' metric emitted to metrics pipeline within 10s of event and visible in the observability UI.
- Burn-rate alerts consult signal_confidence; in canary run we observe >=30% reduction in noise pages across test tenants.
- Autoresolve actions are logged and visible in audit events; on-call can opt out per incident.
- Runbook and dashboard published with links and playbook steps.

Implementation notes / design decisions:
1) Tracing hook placement: implement as a lightweight interceptor in the ingress gateway (sidecar path for private) to avoid adding latency. Enrichment values are lookups to a cached routing metadata store refreshed every 30s.
2) Fusion window: 120s sliding window with priority to latest 30s for high-sensitivity cases. We aggregate per-customer and per-model-variant to avoid global churn.
3) Signal scoring: join factors - burst amplitude, error-rate delta vs baseline, correlated log signatures (>=2 matching error signatures), and trace-sample rate. Score scaled 0.0-1.0; threshold 0.6 triggers page by default, 0.35-0.6 triggers aggregated alert with no immediate page. Thresholds configurable per project.
4) Autoresolve: only allowed if signal_confidence drops below 0.15 for 5 consecutive minutes and incident has not breached customer-impact whitelist. All autoresolve decisions create an immutable audit log and Slack/PD notification.

Telemetry and observability changes:
- New metrics: signal_confidence, signal_enrichment_rate, fusion_latency_ms.
- New logs: gatekeeper_decision, enrichment_lookup_miss, fusion_correlation_event.
- Dashboards: 'Signal Gatekeeper Overview' and per-tenant slicer.

API / Config knobs:
- feature_flag: gatekeeper.enabled, gatekeeper.sample_rate, gatekeeper.score_thresholds (low/medium/high).
- per-customer override: opt_out_autoresolve=true.

Operational considerations / runbook highlights:
- On-call flow: if page fires but signal_confidence < 0.6, page is routed to 'observability-lite' oncall group with lower escalation cadence; if engineer marks incident as 'true-degradation' the system escalates to SRE.
- Fail-open policy: if correlator fails, alerts should revert to legacy burn-rate behavior and generate a high-priority alarm to engage SRE.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: enrichment lookups could introduce latency. Mitigation: local TTL cache + metrics + circuit-breaker fallback.
- Risk: incorrect fusion thresholds suppress real incidents. Mitigation: start conservative, run extended canary, and include manual escalation override.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: Deploy tracing hook (flagged) + metric emission to canary tenants (20%).
- Week 1: Enable fusion correlator in read-only mode (emit signal_confidence but do not suppress pages).
- Week 2: Pilot conditional suppression for internal tenants (no external客户) and monitor false-negatives.
- Week 3: Expand to 50% hosted, enable autoresolve with 1-hour safety hold.
- Week 4: Full rollout to Dedicated and default rules; collect 30-day metrics for next tuning iteration.

Monitoring and Success metrics:
- Pager reduction (target 40% for noise pages tied to burn-rate)
- False-negative rate (target < 3% relative to gold-standard incident labels)
- Correlator latency (target median < 10s)
- Increase in enriched trace tags present (target 95% for targeted paths)

Notes / Links:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Signal+Gatekeeper+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/3124
- Dashboard (draft): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/signal-gatekeeper/overview
- Runbook: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xAMPLEgatekeeper-runbook
